hints.title: Unfold the faces the path crosses
hints.body: On a flat net, the shortest path between two points is a straight line. There are two short route types to compare: across the base and one triangular face, or across two triangular faces. Reflecting the pyramid gives matching routes on the other side.
hints.recap: Unfolding preserves distances along a surface and turns a surface-path problem into plane geometry.
hints.pitfall: A straight line through the three-dimensional interior is shorter but is not an allowed surface path.
hints.pause: Draw the two triangular faces OPS and OSR joined along OS, and mark the midpoint T of OR.

recall.reminder: Identify a relevant plane or cross-section before calculating lengths in a three-dimensional geometry problem.
Unfolding adjacent flat faces preserves surface lengths. A straight segment is shortest for its chosen face sequence only when it crosses the intended edges and remains inside those faces.

hints.title: Find separations in each net
hints.body: Bisect an equilateral face to find its perpendicular height. In the unfolded pair, mark the midpoint T carefully and calculate the horizontal and vertical separations from P.
hints.recap: Pythagoras applies to the perpendicular separations in a flat net.
hints.pitfall: A midpoint halves each coordinate displacement along its edge; check which distances add across the shared edge.
hints.pause: Calculate each feasible path length from your nets and verify that its straight segment stays on the unfolded faces.

recall.reminder: Pythagoras applies to the perpendicular separations in a flat net.

solution:
1. Flatten the surface route. Unfold faces OPS and OSR about their shared edge OS. Their side lengths are all 20, so both are equilateral.

2. Find the separations. An equilateral face has height 20sin60∘=103. In this net, P is 103 left of OS. Because T is the midpoint of OR, it is 53 right of OS and 5 above P. Thus PT2=(153)2+52=700. The straight segment crosses OS between O and S, so it is a valid path across the two faces.

3. Compare the base route. Unfolding the square base with face OSR instead gives horizontal separation 15 and vertical separation 20+53. Its squared length is 152+(20+53)2=700+2003, which is larger. The reflected routes via the other side have the same respective lengths.

Answer D. The shorter surface distance is 700=107 metres.
knowledgePattern: Unfold competing face routes on an equilateral-sided square pyramid
